title: Reconcile menubar with externally started TongStock services
description: Menubar reports Service Stopped when a manually started or legacy tongstock-server owns port 8080, so Stop is a no-op and Start/Restart can fail. Make lifecycle state authoritative across menubar-managed, unified CLI, and legacy server processes while validating identity before termination.
design: Make the server process authoritative for PID metadata and graceful cleanup. Menubar first validates the PID record, then falls back to configured-port listener discovery plus strict command identity checks for unified and legacy TongStock processes. Expose service identity and PID in /health. Represent verified external services and unrelated port conflicts distinctly; never kill an unverified listener.
acceptance_criteria: Menubar detects a healthy external TongStock server; status distinguishes managed/external service; Stop and Restart terminate a verified TongStock process even without a PID file; unrelated processes on the configured port are never killed; server ownership metadata remains correct across manual and menu starts; external-process regression tests and full Go quality gates pass.
notes: Observed root cause: legacy ./tongstock-server processes started from Trae had no menubar-owned PID, so the UI said stopped. Verified final installed ~/.local/bin/tongstock end-to-end: PID 56326 recorded itself, /health returned service=tongstock and matching PID, 8080 listened, SIGTERM logged graceful shutdown, port released, and PID file was removed. Web was explicitly rebuilt and embedded at install time.
close_reason: Implemented authoritative server PID ownership, health identity, external legacy/unified process discovery, safe port-conflict handling, graceful HTTP shutdown, reliable Web build/install, and full external-process regression coverage. Full Go tests/vet, 5x race tests, Web production build, and installed binary end-to-end start/health/stop verification passed.

title: Package menubar and server as one tongstock CLI
description: Replace the separately installed tongstock-menubar and tongstock-server executables with one multicall tongstock binary. Expose tongstock menubar and tongstock server commands while keeping the HTTP service in a child process so Start/Restart/Stop remain isolated and reliable. Preserve legacy wrappers for compatibility and do not mix existing stockpool/web workspace changes into the commit.
design: Use a multicall tongstock binary with server and menubar Cobra subcommands. The menubar launches its own executable with the server argument, retaining a separate child process for crash isolation. Move implementations into importable internal packages, retain legacy wrappers, and make default build/install/release output only tongstock.
acceptance_criteria: A single installed tongstock binary can launch the menubar and server modes; the menubar starts/restarts itself with the server subcommand and stops only that child; legacy cmd/server and cmd/menubar wrappers still build; installer/Makefile install one binary; lifecycle, CLI, and full Go tests pass.
notes: Installed locally at ~/.local/bin/tongstock. LaunchAgent now runs 'tongstock menubar' and is confirmed running. Existing stockpool/web workspace edits were preserved and not treated as a separate origin operation.
close_reason: Implemented and locally installed the unified tongstock CLI with server and menubar commands; updated lifecycle PID metadata, default build/install, release/CI packaging, docs, and scripts; full Go tests, vet, race tests, builds, help smoke tests, and LaunchAgent verification passed.

title: Fix menubar-managed server lifecycle and installation
description: Menubar Start/Restart/Stop does not reliably manage tongstock-server. Keep the UI and HTTP server isolated, make process discovery and graceful termination reliable, install the matched binaries together, and add regression coverage without disturbing unrelated workspace changes.
design: Keep menubar and HTTP server as separate processes for crash isolation and so Stop Service does not terminate the UI. Fix distribution by installing both binaries together. Replace fire-and-forget lifecycle handling with child reaping, zombie detection, PID validation, and bounded graceful-stop/forced-stop waits before restart.
acceptance_criteria: The menubar installer deploys both tongstock-menubar and tongstock-server; Start reaps exited children and never reports zombies as running; Restart waits until the prior server exits before launching the replacement; Stop terminates the owned server, clears only its PID record, and automated lifecycle tests plus Go quality gates pass.
notes: Observed live failure mode: ~/.tongstock/server.pid pointed to PID 6479, shown by ps as <defunct> with tongstock-menubar as parent. Existing code never called Cmd.Wait, so Signal(0) misclassified the zombie as running. Installer also built only tongstock-menubar, leaving the server dependency stale or missing.
close_reason: Fixed menubar lifecycle management: child processes are reaped, zombies are treated as stopped, PID ownership is validated, graceful stop waits before forced termination, restart waits for the old process, logs are preserved, installer builds both binaries, and lifecycle/race/full Go tests pass.
